chunks: Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Sama'ah who said, 'I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying,'

'Do not consider much good as abundant, and do not consider few sins as paltry, for verily few sins gather until they become many. And fear Allah in private and in public, until you give half of yourselves [to Him]. And hasten to the obedience of Allah, be truthful in speech, and fulfill the trust, for indeed that is for your own benefit. Do not oppress [anyone] and do not enter into that which is not permissible for you, for indeed that is to your detriment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of small sins accumulating according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) warns against the cumulative nature of minor sins and the complacency regarding good deeds, urging believers to maintain God-consciousness in both private and public spheres. He emphasizes hastening to obedience, truthfulness, and fulfilling trusts as essential components of spiritual integrity, while cautioning against oppression and entering into impermissible matters. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on the balance between inner piety and outward action, highlighting the importance of consistency in small deeds.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 10.ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Samāʿah who said, “I heard Abā alḤasan Mūsā (a) saying, ‘

Do not consider [your] many good deeds as abundant, and do not consider [your] few sins as paltry, for verily sins that are few keep accumulating until they become many. And fear Allah in [both] private and public, until you behave in a fair manner [with others]. Hasten towards the obedience of Allah, be truthful in speech, and fulfil the trust [that is entrusted to you], for indeed this is for your own benefit. Do not oppress [anyone] and do not enter into that which is impermissible for you, as that is to your detriment.’”
